questions.questionText: What is the average actual production per town across the 5 towns? (in thousand garments, correct to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: Sum of actual production = 1839. Average = 1839 ÷ 5 = 367.8.
questions.shortcut: Add the bar-chart values and divide by the number of bars.

questions.questionText: The actual production of Karur is what percentage of its annual production target? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Both values come from the combined data: annual production target = 420 and actual production = 357 (thousand garments). Percentage = 357 ÷ 420 × 100 = 85.0%.
questions.shortcut: Part ÷ whole × 100, where the whole is the Table figure.

questions.questionText: The peak load supplied of Ennore is what percentage of its installed capacity? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Both values come from the combined data: installed capacity = 720 and peak load supplied = 540 (MW). Percentage = 540 ÷ 720 × 100 = 75.0%.
questions.shortcut: Part ÷ whole × 100, where the whole is the Table figure.

questions.questionText: What is the ratio of installed capacity to peak load supplied for Ennore in its simplest form?
questions.explanation: installed capacity : peak load supplied = 720 : 540. HCF = 180, so the ratio is 4:3.
questions.shortcut: Divide both numbers by their HCF; keep Table first, Bar second.

questions.questionText: What is the average seats filled per college across the 5 colleges? (in seats, correct to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: Sum of seats filled = 3034. Average = 3034 ÷ 5 = 606.8.
questions.shortcut: Add the bar-chart values and divide by the number of bars.

questions.questionText: What is the total shortfall of seats filled below seats sanctioned, summed over all colleges? (in seats)
questions.explanation: Total seats sanctioned = 3720; total seats filled = 3034. Shortfall = 3720 − 3034 = 686.
questions.shortcut: Subtract the two column totals instead of five separate gaps.

questions.questionText: The on-time trains of Palakkad is what percentage of its scheduled trains? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Both values come from the combined data: scheduled trains = 180 and on-time trains = 162 (trains per day). Percentage = 162 ÷ 180 × 100 = 90.0%.
questions.shortcut: Part ÷ whole × 100, where the whole is the Table figure.

questions.questionText: What is the average beds occupied per hospital across the 5 hospitals? (in beds, correct to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: Sum of beds occupied = 1481. Average = 1481 ÷ 5 = 296.2.
questions.shortcut: Add the bar-chart values and divide by the number of bars.

questions.questionText: The milk actually procured of Kolhapur Gokul is what percentage of its procurement capacity? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Both values come from the combined data: procurement capacity = 480 and milk actually procured = 360 (thousand litres per day). Percentage = 360 ÷ 480 × 100 = 75.0%.
questions.shortcut: Part ÷ whole × 100, where the whole is the Table figure.

questions.questionText: Coimbatore's annual production target forms what percentage of the total annual production target of all towns? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Total annual production target = 2100. Share = 540 ÷ 2100 × 100 = 25.7%.
questions.shortcut: Use the Table column total as the base.

questions.questionText: By what percentage is the actual production of Coimbatore more than that of Karur? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Difference = 486 − 357 = 129. Percentage more = 129 ÷ 357 × 100 = 36.1% (base is the smaller entity).
questions.shortcut: 'More than' means the base is the one after 'than'.

questions.questionText: By what percentage is the peak load supplied of Neyveli more than that of Tuticorin? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Difference = 1320 − 945 = 375. Percentage more = 375 ÷ 945 × 100 = 39.7% (base is the smaller entity).
questions.shortcut: 'More than' means the base is the one after 'than'.

questions.questionText: Vallur's installed capacity forms what percentage of the total installed capacity of all power stations? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Total installed capacity = 5760. Share = 1500 ÷ 5760 × 100 = 26.0%.
questions.shortcut: Use the Table column total as the base.

questions.questionText: For how many of the 5 colleges is the seats filled higher than the average seats filled of all 5?
questions.explanation: Average = 3034 ÷ 5 = 606.8. Values above it: Kaveri Institute, Vaigai Institute = 2.
questions.shortcut: Find the mean once, then scan the bars.

questions.questionText: By what percentage is the seats filled of Kaveri Institute more than that of Nilgiri Tech? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Difference = 810 − 570 = 240. Percentage more = 240 ÷ 570 × 100 = 42.1% (base is the smaller entity).
questions.shortcut: 'More than' means the base is the one after 'than'.

questions.questionText: Madurai's scheduled trains forms what percentage of the total scheduled trains of all divisions? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Total scheduled trains = 800. Share = 120 ÷ 800 × 100 = 15.0%.
questions.shortcut: Use the Table column total as the base.

questions.questionText: Taking Chennai and Palakkad together, the combined on-time trains is what percentage of their combined scheduled trains? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Combined on-time trains = 204+162 = 366; combined scheduled trains = 240+180 = 420. Ratio = 87.1%. (Averaging the two separate percentages would be wrong.)
questions.shortcut: Add numerators and denominators first; never average percentages with different bases.

questions.questionText: For how many of the 5 divisions is the on-time trains higher than the average on-time trains of all 5?
questions.explanation: Average = 685 ÷ 5 = 137.0. Values above it: Chennai, Palakkad = 2.

questions.questionText: By what percentage is the beds occupied of Vellore more than that of Thanjavur? (Correct to one decimal place.)

questions.shortcut: 'More than' means the base is the one after 'than'.

questions.questionText: Find the difference between the highest and the lowest value of (actual production ÷ annual production target) × 100 among the towns. (Correct to one decimal place.)

questions.questionText: Find the difference between the highest and the lowest value of (beds occupied ÷ sanctioned beds) × 100 among the hospitals. (Correct to one decimal place.)

questions.questionText: Find the difference between the highest and the lowest value of (milk actually procured ÷ procurement capacity) × 100 among the cooperatives. (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Percentages: Anand Sahakari 90.00%, Kolhapur Gokul 75.00%, Erode Aavin 87.50%, Nashik Vikas 80.00%, Hubli Nandini 94.00%. Difference = 94.00 − 75.00 = 19.0 percentage points.
